clues.title: Bollard: Bollard
text: Germany uses these black and white bollards, with white and light-grey reflectors. The reflector will be orange on bollards next to intersections. They sometimes have plates containing the road number, and potentially other useful information. Many bollards also feature blue attachments on the side.

NOTE: Many European countries have similar bollards, however most will have different coloured reflectors. Luxembourg uses almost identical bollards, but they have 3 bolts instead of 2 on the reflector.

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Sylt
text: The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.
NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

clues.title: Google car: Car Meta - Gen 3 Black Car
text: You can find a Generation 3 black car in this safari park southeast of Bielefeld.
You can commonly see 4x4s painted with a zebra pattern in the park.
NOTE: This car is unique to this park within all of Europe.

clues.title: Language: German
text: German is a Germanic language related to Dutch. The German language uses the special letters **Ä, Ö, Ü** and **ß**.
The German word for street is **Straße**.
The German word for road is **Weg** (same as Dutch).
Alongside Germany, German is the majority language in Austria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein, and has regional majority in eastern Belgium and the Italian province of South Tyrol.
